issues.description: The problem statement intermittently refers to a method named getFeedingSound() (used in the song placeholders and the description of feedAllAnimals) while the UML, tasks, template intent, and the provided solution implement and expect messageOnFeed() as the abstract feeding method. This name mismatch in the specification vs. the implemented solution will confuse students about which method name/signature to implement and which method feedAllAnimals / singFarmSong should call.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Update the problem statement to refer to messageOnFeed() everywhere (including the song placeholders and the feedAllAnimals description) or alternatively rename the abstract method in the UML/template/solution to getFeedingSound(). Ensure the template and example solution use the same method name so students know which method to implement and invoke.

issues.description: The problem statement inconsistently refers to the animal feeding method as getFeedingSound() in Part 2, while the UML, the Animal implementation guidance, the template/solution code and tests use messageOnFeed(). This mismatch can confuse students about which method to implement and will likely cause compilation/test failures if they follow the getFeedingSound() name from the textual description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent with the UML and code by replacing all occurrences of getFeedingSound() with messageOnFeed(), and clarify example return values accordingly (e.g., 'messageOnFeed() should return "Arf Arf!"' for Seal).
